summary: Controllable, durable and spinny, with a linear, consistent feel and good value. The main downsides are a high, bouncy arc and catapult that some find hard to control, and a few find it too fast or lacking spin on serves.

Very spinny and durable, with a tacky topsheet that many find controllable and good in the short game. Downsides are a hard, fast feel that some find hard to control, especially on the backhand, plus grip that fades for a few and some complaints about weight and price. Rewards solid technique.

Controllable, spinny and forgiving, with a consistent feel and good durability, and often recommended for beginners and developing players. Complaints are minor: some find it too bouncy or fast at max, others find it slow with capped spin, and a few note its weight.

Very spinny, controllable and linear, with a low throw, a hard sponge and good durability, though it is slow. It is demanding: many find it hard to control without full-body strokes and good technique, and a few see the tack fade. Often boosted, and favoured by looping players.

Fast, spinny and great in feel, loved for loops. The main complaint is that it is bouncy and hard to control, particularly in the short game, blocking and for less experienced players. Many also say the grip fades after a few months, and it is pricey.

Fast, spinny and very durable, with a grippy but non-tacky topsheet and a hard sponge. Control is the main sticking point: many find it hard to control or too fast, especially for blocking and touch shots, though some find it steadier than Tenergy 05. Best for strong, aggressive players, mostly on the backhand.

Controllable, forgiving and good value, often called a cheaper, tamer alternative to Tenergy 05. The main downside is bounciness, with some finding it too fast or springy, especially beginners, and several struggling to get backspin on serves. Durability reports are mixed.

A fast, crisp carbon-feel blade with good feel that many like, especially on the backhand. The main complaint is that it is too fast and low in dwell, leading to hard-to-control shots, so many reviewers say it suits players with solid strokes rather than beginners.

A tacky hybrid with strong spin, good control and a good short game, and it holds up well. Weight is the main complaint, with many calling it heavy. Others note the high throw and hard sponge, so it is not ideal for beginners.

Soft, forgiving and controllable, a popular backhand rubber and good for beginners. Downsides are that some find it too soft or mushy, bottoming out and slow, and a few find it bouncy or hard to control. Some prefer regular Rakza 7.

Very fast and spinny, with good durability and strong counterplay and blocking for those who can handle it. Many find it hard to control or too fast, with little dwell and a weak short game, and it is expensive. Suits advanced players with full strokes.

Very fast and spinny, often picked as a cheaper alternative to Tenergy 05. The main complaints are grip that fades quickly, often within weeks to a couple of months, and a bouncy feel that is hard to control. Durability reports are mixed, with some getting long use.

Usually described as a slower, softer and more controllable relative of Dignics 09C, with good spin and a forgiving feel. Complaints are scattered: some find it too slow or mushy, particularly on all-wood blades, and a few say the grip fades quickly. Suits players who find Dignics too fast.

A softer, more forgiving take on Fastarc G-1, with good control, decent spin and solid durability. Popular on the backhand. Complaints are few: a handful find it too bouncy, mushy or slow, with an odd throw angle.

Very spinny and controlled, a slow rubber that forces full strokes, and some credit it with improving technique. Downsides are a hard, unforgiving sponge that is demanding, especially for beginners, plus tack that fades so it often needs boosting.

An all-wood blade that is slow, soft and very controllable with a good feel, popular with beginners and improving players at a fair price. Some find it lacks power and speed, and several dislike the thin handle or sweet spot.

A soft, forgiving and cheap rubber with plenty of control, durable and good for blocking and backhand play. Some find it too soft or mushy, and it lacks speed and spin for forehands or stronger players. Edges can crumble.

Fast and spinny with strong grip, a firmer topsheet than Vega Pro, and good control for many. The main complaint is that the catapult and spin sensitivity make it hard to control for some, along with a hard topsheet and extra weight.

A fast, spinny and cheap rubber that is controllable enough for developing players. Reports on durability are mixed, with some sheets lasting many months and others losing spin or crumbling, and a few find it too fast or hard to activate. Few real complaints.

A very tacky, hard-sponge rubber that is extremely spinny with a low throw and good control. Grip fading is the main complaint, with many boosting it and replacing sheets often, though some report sheets staying tacky for months. Hard and physically demanding, so better for strong players.
